newsitem.title: UK: Possible 15th British mad cow victim dies.
newsitem.headline: Possible 15th British mad cow victim dies.

text.p: British health officials declined to confirm on Tuesday whether a 15th victim of the human form of mad cow disease had died.
The Express newspaper quoted relatives as saying 25-year-old Adrian Hodgkinson had succumbed to a new variant of the brain-wasting Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD).
But British health officials said they could not comment on individual cases.

"There are 14 confirmed cases of new variant CJD and one probable case, and one confirmed case in France," said Dr Richard Knight of the National CJD Surveillance Unit in Edinburgh. CJD can only be diagnosed with certainty by a brain biopsy or autopsy after death.
But the symptoms of the new variant include increasing lack of coordination, ending in brain failure and certain death.

CJD usually affects one in a million, usually elderly, people because of its long incubation period. But a new variant identified last march has been linked to the epidemic of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE or mad cow disease) that swept British herds in the 1980s.
British admission that the new type of CJD, which affects younger people and has a slightly different pattern in the brain, caused the European Union to ban exports of British beef.
